Sources.Claim: The documented NetUserModalsSet information levels cover password modal fields such as minimum length, maximum/minimum age, forced logoff, history and lockout; complexity is not listed.
Password complexity is a security policy setting in the Account Policies/Password Policy area; Microsoft documents its enabled behavior and values.
Secedit export can merge local and domain policy; secedit configure applies security settings defined in a database for selected areas; generaterollback emits a rollback template.

CandidateDesign.Status: Investigation only; no module, catalog operation or supported target added.
CandidateDesign.Hypothesis: A minimal security template containing only [System Access] PasswordComplexity and an isolated security database may permit a narrowly scoped local writer, with secedit-generated rollback.
CandidateDesign.Inference: Microsoft documents applying settings defined in a database and generating rollback templates. This suggests a testable path but does not prove an isolated database/template changes only the requested policy, preserves unrelated local/domain policy, or restores an originally undefined local value exactly.
CandidateDesign.PotentialObservationSplit: Capture local policy without /mergedpolicy separately from merged effective policy; do not treat the merged result as the locally owned value or infer that domain/MDM policy will allow a local value to take effect.

RequiredTests: Windows 11 and Server 2025: baseline local value Enabled, Disabled and Not defined, then apply, repeat, conflict refusal and exact restore.
Prove a local-only change and preserve unrelated System Access values and other securitypolicy areas byte/semantically as applicable.
Test effective domain/MDM policy precedence and refuse or report partial when the effective value differs from the locally owned setting.
Verify failure after pre-change capture and before/after secedit configure, including rollback-template validity and recovery.
Refuse domain controllers and unknown roles; record elevation and restart/refresh behavior without changing passwords.

Resolved: The current NetUserModalsSet backend is not a password-complexity writer.
Deferred: Implement a one-setting secedit candidate only after isolated disposable-VM proof of exact ownership and rollback.
All native Windows 11/Server 2025, local/managed policy, unrelated-field, failure and recovery acceptance.
Partial: No legacy password-complexity outcome closes; no supported target or catalog operation is added.

Estimate.Adjustment: Unchanged because API/source research adds no setting implementation or native acceptance.
